title: Simple Tomato Spaghetti
description: Five ingredients, fifteen minutes, and better than any jar.
steps: Get the pasta boiling in well-salted water before you start anything else.
Warm the oil with the garlic and pepper flakes over medium heat 2 minutes, until the garlic is just turning pale gold.
Tear in the basil stalks - they carry more flavor than the leaves - then add the tomatoes and salt and simmer hard for 8 minutes, crushing them with a spoon.
Drain the pasta a minute early, saving a cup of the water, and tip it straight into the sauce.
Toss over the heat for a full minute with a splash of pasta water. This is where the sauce goes from sitting on the pasta to clinging to it.
Tear in the basil leaves, add half the Parmesan and serve with the rest on top.

title: Chicken in Milk
description: A whole chicken slow-roasted in milk with lemon zest, sage and cinnamon.
steps: Heat the oven to 375F. Pat the chicken dry and season it all over.
Brown it in the butter and oil in a snug casserole, turning, until golden on all sides. Pour off most of the fat but leave the browned bits.
Add the cinnamon stick, sage, lemon zest strips and unpeeled garlic, then pour in the milk around the bird.
Roast uncovered for 1 1/2 hours, basting a few times. Do not be alarmed when the milk splits into curds - that curdling is the entire point, and it becomes the sauce.
The chicken is done when the thigh reads 175F and the milk has reduced to golden, lemony curds.
Rest 10 minutes, then pull the chicken apart and spoon the curds and garlic over. Serve with bread or greens.

title: Perfect Roast Chicken
description: A whole chicken roasted on a bed of vegetables with lemon and herbs.
steps: Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes early and heat the oven to 425F. A cold bird cooks unevenly.
Pile the carrots, celery, onions and garlic in the middle of a roasting tray - they act as a trivet, so the bird roasts rather than stews, and they flavor the gravy.
Pierce the lemon all over with a knife and microwave it 40 seconds, then push it into the cavity with half the herbs. The warm lemon steams the inside of the bird as it cooks.
Rub the chicken all over with olive oil, salt and pepper and scatter the rest of the herbs on top. Set it on the vegetables.
Roast about 1 1/2 hours, until the juices from the thigh run clear and a thermometer reads 175F there.
Rest on a board 15 minutes, loosely covered, then carve and serve with the vegetables and pan juices.

title: Sausage and Fennel Pappardelle
description: Sausage meat crumbled into a fennel seed and red wine ragu.
steps: Crush the fennel seeds roughly in a mortar or under a pan - whole seeds are harsh, crushed ones perfume the whole sauce.
Fry the sausage meat in the oil over high heat, breaking it into chunks rather than crumbs, 8 minutes until well browned.
Add the fennel seeds, pepper flakes, onion and garlic and cook 6 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble away almost completely, scraping the pan.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer 15 minutes while the pappardelle cooks.
Toss the drained pasta through the sauce with a ladle of pasta water, then finish with Parmesan and parsley.

title: Beef Stew with Dumplings
description: Slow-cooked beef and root vegetables under fluffy suet dumplings.
ingredients: 1/2 cup shredded suet or cold butter
steps: Toss the beef with the flour, salt and pepper, then brown it hard in the oil in batches. Crowding the pan gives you grey meat and no flavor base.
Add the onions, carrots, celery and parsnips and cook 10 minutes, then the garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Pour in the ale and reduce by half, then add the broth, rosemary and bay leaves.
Cover and cook at 325F for 2 hours until the beef is tender.

Rub the suet or cold butter into the self-rising flour with a pinch of salt, then stir in the cold water to a soft, shaggy dough. Roll into 10 balls, handling them as little as possible - overworked dumplings go heavy.
Sit the dumplings on top of the stew, cover and cook 25 minutes, then uncover for 10 minutes so the tops brown. Finish with parsley.

title: Proper Pesto Pasta
description: Pesto pounded in a mortar, loosened with pasta water and never cooked.
steps: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden, then cool them. Raw pine nuts taste flat and slightly resinous.
Pound the basil, pine nuts, garlic and a pinch of salt to a rough paste in a mortar, or pulse briefly in a processor. Pulse only - running the motor heats the basil and turns it black.
Stir in both cheeses, then the olive oil in a stream, and season with pepper and lemon juice.
Boil the pasta in well-salted water, adding the diced potato at the start and the green beans for the last 4 minutes. Cooking them in with the pasta is the Ligurian way and makes it a complete dish.
Drain, reserving a cup of water, then toss everything with the pesto off the heat. Never heat pesto in a pan - it dulls and goes bitter.
Loosen with pasta water until it coats every piece and serve at once.

title: Easy Mushroom Risotto
description: A forgiving risotto built on dried porcini stock and finished with lemon.
steps: Soak the porcini in a cup of the hot broth 20 minutes, then chop them and strain the liquid back into the pot of broth. Keep the broth at a bare simmer throughout.
Tear rather than slice the fresh mushrooms - ragged edges brown better - and fry them in the olive oil over high heat 6 minutes until deeply colored. Set aside.
Sweat the onion and celery in 2 tbsp butter 8 minutes without browning, then add the garlic and the rice and toast 2 minutes.
Add the wine and stir until absorbed, then add the hot broth a ladleful at a time, stirring often, for about 18 minutes until the rice is al dente with a creamy sauce.
Fold in the chopped porcini and most of the fried mushrooms near the end.
Off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the Parmesan hard - this is what makes it glossy - then add the lemon zest, thyme and parsley. Serve immediately.

title: Lamb Kofta Flatbreads
description: Spiced lamb skewers with yogurt, pickled onion and herbs in flatbread.
steps: Toss the sliced red onion with the vinegar and a pinch of salt and leave it to pickle while you cook - 20 minutes is enough to transform it.
Knead the lamb with the spices, garlic, herbs, salt and pepper for 2-3 minutes until it turns tacky. That stickiness is what holds the kofta together on the skewer.
Press the mixture around skewers in long sausage shapes, or just shape it into flat ovals.
Cook on a very hot griddle or grill 10-12 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until charred outside and just cooked through.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Warm the flatbreads, spread with yogurt, and pile on the kofta, lettuce, pickled onion and a dusting of sumac.

title: Mediterranean Veg Traybake
description: One tray of summer vegetables roasted with garlic, herbs and vinegar.
ingredients: 2 red bell peppers, cut in chunks
1 head garlic, cloves separated and unpeeled
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Cut everything into generous, similar-sized chunks so nothing burns while the rest is still raw.
Toss all the vegetables with the unpeeled garlic cloves, olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper in a large roasting tray.
Spread them into one layer. If the tray is crowded, use two - crowded vegetables steam and stay pale.
Roast 40-45 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges and completely soft.
Squeeze the soft garlic out of a few skins and mash it through the vegetables, then toss everything with the vinegar while hot.
Tear in the basil, crumble the feta over and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Fish Pie
description: Smoked and white fish in parsley sauce under a mashed potato crust.
ingredients: 2 1/2 cups whole milk, for the sauce
steps: Boil the potatoes until tender, drain, then let them steam dry in the pan for a minute before mashing with 3 tbsp butter and the warm milk. Dry potatoes make a mash that holds its shape on top.

Melt the remaining butter, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the 2 1/2 cups milk gradually and simmer until it thickens. Add the mustard powder, nutmeg, half the cheddar, the parsley, lemon zest and seasoning.
Wilt the spinach in a dry pan, squeeze it dry and scatter it over the base of a baking dish.
Add the raw fish, haddock, shrimp and quartered eggs, then pour the sauce over. The fish goes in raw - it poaches in the sauce in the oven, and pre-cooking it means dry, chalky pieces.
Spoon the mash over in dollops and spread gently to seal the edges, then rough up the top with a fork and scatter the rest of the cheddar.
Bake at 400F for 40-45 minutes until bubbling at the edges and golden on top. Rest 10 minutes.

title: Crispy Salmon with Smashed Greens
description: Crisp-skinned salmon over peas and beans smashed with mint and lemon.
ingredients: 4 salmon fillets, skin on (6 oz each)
steps: Pat the salmon skin completely dry and season it. Dry skin is the only way to get it crisp.
Lay the fillets skin-side down in the oil in a cold nonstick pan, then turn the heat to medium-high and press them flat for 15 seconds.
Cook 6-8 minutes on the skin without moving them, until the flesh has turned opaque three quarters of the way up. Flip for just 60 seconds.
Meanwhile boil the peas and green beans 4 minutes, then drain.
Fry the garlic in the butter 1 minute, add the greens and crush them roughly with a masher, leaving plenty of texture.
Stir the mint, lemon zest and juice through the greens, season, and serve the salmon skin-side up on top with the feta scattered over.

title: Chicken Cacciatore
description: Chicken thighs braised with red wine, olives and rosemary.
steps: Pat the chicken dry, season well and brown it skin-side down in the oil 7 minutes, then 3 minutes on the other side. Set aside.
Cook the onions in the same pan 8 minutes, then add the garlic, rosemary and pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the anchovies and mash them into the oil until they dissolve. They will not taste fishy - they are what gives the braise its savory depth.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, scraping up everything stuck to the pan.
Add the tomatoes, olives and bay leaves, then nestle the chicken back in skin-side up and above the liquid so the skin stays crisp.
Braise uncovered at 375F for 45 minutes. Discard the bay leaves and rosemary stems and finish with torn basil.

title: Aubergine Parmigiana
description: Grilled eggplant layered with tomato, basil and Parmesan - no breadcrumbs, no frying.
steps: Griddle the eggplant slices in a dry hot pan, in batches, 3 minutes per side until charred and softened. Grilling rather than frying keeps the dish from turning greasy and is the key difference here.
Cook the onions in the olive oil 10 minutes, then add the garlic and pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, oregano, salt and pepper and simmer 25 minutes until thick. Tear in half the basil.
Layer in a baking dish: sauce, eggplant, Parmesan, basil. Repeat three times, keeping the sauce sparing so it does not go sloppy.
Finish with the torn mozzarella, the remaining Parmesan and the breadcrumbs.
Bake at 400F for 35-40 minutes until bubbling and browned. Rest 15 minutes before cutting.

title: Minestrone
description: A big pot of vegetables, beans and pasta, finished with pesto.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) cannellini beans, drained
steps: Render the pancetta in the olive oil, then add the onions, carrots and celery and cook 12 minutes until soft and sweet. This slow start is where the body of the soup comes from.
Add the garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes, then the tomatoes.
Mash one can of the beans and add them with the whole beans, the broth and the Parmesan rind. Simmer 20 minutes - the mashed beans thicken it naturally.
Add the zucchini and cabbage and cook 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook until al dente. If you are making it ahead, cook the pasta separately so it does not swell overnight.
Fish out the Parmesan rind, season, and serve with a spoonful of pesto stirred into each bowl and plenty of Parmesan.

title: Chicken Souvlaki Wraps
description: Griddled oregano chicken in flatbread with tzatziki and crunchy salad.
steps: Marinate the chicken in the oil, lemon juice, half the garlic, the oregano, salt and pepper for at least 1 hour.
Make the tzatziki: squeeze every drop of water out of the grated cucumber, then stir it into the yogurt with the remaining garlic and the dill. Wet cucumber makes watery tzatziki.
Cook the chicken on a very hot griddle 6-7 minutes per side until charred and 175F inside. Thighs are far more forgiving than breast over this kind of heat.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice into strips.
Warm the flatbreads briefly on the griddle until pliable.
Spread with tzatziki and build with the chicken, romaine, tomato and red onion. Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Spanish Chicken Traybake
description: Chicken, chorizo and potatoes roasted together with smoked paprika.
ingredients: 2 red bell peppers, cut in chunks
1 head garlic, cloves separated and unpeeled
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the potatoes, peppers, onions and unpeeled garlic with half the oil, the paprika, cayenne, oregano, salt and pepper in a large roasting tray.
Rub the chicken with the rest of the oil and the remaining spices and set it skin-side up on top of the vegetables.
Tuck the chorizo slices in among the vegetables. As it roasts it releases paprika-red fat that seasons everything in the tray - that is the whole mechanism of the dish.
Roast 35 minutes, then squeeze the lemon halves over and tuck them in.
Roast 15-20 minutes more until the chicken skin is dark and crisp and the thighs read 175F.
Rest 5 minutes, scatter with parsley and serve straight from the tray.

title: Slow-Cooked Lamb Shoulder
description: Lamb shoulder cooked for five hours until it falls apart under a fork.
steps: Heat the oven to 450F. Score the lamb fat in a crosshatch, rub it all over with the oil, salt, pepper, cumin and paprika, and push rosemary sprigs into the slashes.
Scatter the onions, carrots and halved garlic heads in a deep roasting tray, set the lamb on top and roast 30 minutes to brown it.
Pour the broth and wine into the tray around - not over - the lamb, then cover the whole thing tightly with foil.
Drop the oven to 300F and cook 4 to 4 1/2 hours. Do not check it often; every time you lift the foil you lose the steam that is doing the work.
It is ready when the meat pulls away from the bone with no resistance at all. If it resists, it needs another 30 minutes - this cut cannot be rushed.
Uncover and roast 20 minutes at 425F to crisp the top. Shred the meat, skim the pan juices, and serve with mint and lemon juice stirred through.

title: Beef Lasagne
description: A long-simmered beef ragu layered with bechamel and Parmesan.
steps: Render the pancetta in the oil, then brown both meats hard. Add the onions, carrots and celery and cook 12 minutes, then the garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes.

Add the wine and reduce by half, then the tomatoes, oregano, rosemary and seasoning. Simmer uncovered 1 1/2 hours until thick and dark. A watery ragu gives you a sloppy lasagne, so let it reduce properly.
Make the bechamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the warm milk gradually and simmer 5 minutes until it coats a spoon. Season with nutmeg and salt.
Boil the noodles 2 minutes short of the package time and lay them flat on oiled trays.
Layer in a deep dish: ragu, noodles, bechamel, Parmesan. Repeat four times, finishing with bechamel, the torn mozzarella and the last of the Parmesan.
Bake at 375F for 45 minutes until browned and bubbling. Rest a full 30 minutes before cutting - this is what lets it hold a slice.

title: Easy Flatbreads
description: Two-ingredient yogurt flatbreads cooked in a dry pan. No yeast, no waiting.
steps: Mix the self-rising flour, yogurt and salt into a dough. It comes together in about a minute - if it is sticky add a little flour, if dry add a spoon more yogurt.
Knead on a floured surface just 2 minutes until smooth. There is no yeast here, so no rising time and no over-proving to worry about.
Divide into 6 and roll each piece out to about 1/4 inch thick.
Cook in a dry hot pan 2-3 minutes per side, until puffed in places and charred in spots. A dry pan, not an oiled one, is what gives the blistering.
Mix the melted butter with the garlic and parsley.
Brush the hot flatbreads with the garlic butter and keep them stacked in a towel so they stay soft.

title: Tray-Baked Sea Bass
description: Whole bass baked over potatoes, tomatoes and olives in one tray.
ingredients: 2 whole sea bass (1 1/2 lb each), cleaned
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the potato slices with half the oil, salt and pepper in a large roasting tray and roast 20 minutes to get them going - fish and raw potatoes cannot start at the same time.
Add the tomatoes, olives, onion and garlic and toss.
Score the fish skin three times per side, pat dry, and season inside and out. Stuff the cavities with lemon slices and oregano.
Set the fish on top of the vegetables, drizzle with the remaining oil and the lemon juice.
Bake 22-25 minutes, until the flesh at the thickest point is opaque and pulls cleanly from the bone.
Rest 5 minutes, scatter with parsley, and lift the fillets off the bone at the table.

title: Jerk Chicken
description: Chicken in a scotch bonnet, allspice and thyme marinade, grilled hard.
steps: Blend the scotch bonnets, scallions, garlic, ginger, allspice, thyme, cinnamon, nutmeg, soy sauce, brown sugar, lime juice, oil and salt into a thick paste. Wear gloves - scotch bonnets will burn your hands and anything you touch afterwards.
Start with two peppers if you are unsure. Four makes a genuinely fierce jerk.
Score the chicken pieces and rub the paste in everywhere, including under the skin. Marinate at least 4 hours and ideally overnight.
Set up a grill for two-zone cooking. Cook the chicken over the cool side with the lid down for 35-40 minutes, turning occasionally.
Move it over the hot zone for the last 5-8 minutes to char. The sugar in the marinade burns fast, so do this at the end and watch it.
Rest 10 minutes and serve with lime wedges and rice.

title: Easy Chocolate Pots
description: Three-ingredient chocolate mousse pots set in the fridge.
steps: Put the chopped chocolate in a bowl with the salt.
Heat the 1 1/2 cups cream with the sugar until steaming but not boiling, then pour it over the chocolate.
Leave it alone for 2 full minutes before touching it. Stirring too early is what makes a grainy, split ganache.
Stir from the center outwards until completely smooth and glossy, then add the vanilla and rum.
Pour into 6 small glasses and chill at least 2 hours until set.
Whip the remaining cream to soft peaks, spoon it on top, and finish with cocoa and pistachios.

title: Summer Berry Crumble
description: Mixed berries under an oat and almond crumble topping.
ingredients: 2 lb mixed berries, fresh or frozen
steps: Heat the oven to 375F. Toss the berries with the sugar, cornstarch, lemon zest and juice and tip them into a baking dish. The cornstarch is what stops the juices flooding out as syrup.
Mix the flour, oats, brown sugar, almonds, cinnamon and salt.
Rub the cold butter into the dry mixture with your fingertips until it clumps into pebbles of different sizes. Uneven clumps give a far better texture than a uniform sandy crumb.
Scatter the topping over the fruit without pressing it down - it needs air to crisp.
Bake 40-45 minutes until the topping is deep golden and the fruit is bubbling up thickly at the edges.
Rest 15 minutes and serve warm with cream.

title: Gnocchi with Tomato and Basil
description: Pan-fried gnocchi in a quick tomato sauce with torn mozzarella.
steps: Fry the gnocchi straight from the package in 2 tbsp of the oil over medium-high heat, in a single layer, 4-5 minutes until golden and crisp on the outside. Frying rather than boiling gives a far better texture - crisp outside, pillowy inside.
Push them to one side, add the remaining oil, garlic and pepper flakes and cook 1 minute.
Tear in the basil stalks, then add the tomatoes and seasoning and simmer 10 minutes, crushing them with a spoon.
Fold the gnocchi back through the sauce and warm through 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat, scatter the torn mozzarella over, and cover for 2 minutes so it softens into strands without melting away.
Tear in the basil leaves, add the Parmesan and serve straight from the pan.

title: Grilled Mackerel with Couscous
description: Oily mackerel fillets grilled hard, served on herb and lemon couscous.
ingredients: 1/3 cup olive oil, for the couscous
steps: Pour the boiling broth over the couscous, cover tightly and leave 10 minutes, then fork it through thoroughly, breaking up every clump.
Fold in the herbs, cucumber, tomatoes, the 1/3 cup olive oil and the lemon juice, and season well.
Score the mackerel skin twice per fillet and pat completely dry. Rub with the 3 tbsp oil and the cumin, paprika, cayenne, salt and pepper.
Get a griddle or grill properly hot. Cook the fillets skin-side down 3-4 minutes without moving them, until the skin is crisp and releases on its own.
Flip for just 1 minute. Mackerel is thin and oily - it cooks fast and goes dry quickly.
Serve the fillets skin-side up on the couscous with the feta scattered over and more lemon.
